articles.title: Lewis Hamilton aims to extend career till early 2030s so he can race in African Grand Prix
articles.summary: 41-year-old set on ‘dream to be able to race in Africa’ Rwanda to host despite criticism of human rights record. Lewis Hamilton has said he hopes to remain racing in Formula One until he can take part in the African Grand Prix which is set to take place in Rwanda in the 2030s.
body: Last week F1 confirmed Rwanda was to host the African Grand Prix having concluded a 10-year agreement for the meeting on a purpose-built circuit, with the first race set for the early 2030s. It is lined up to be held on a circuit in Bugesera, 25 miles south of the capital, Kigali, which has yet to be constructed and marks a return to the African continent for the first time since it last held a race at Kyalami, South Africa in 1993.

Hamilton has been championing a race in Africa for some time. The 41-year-old is understood to be currently contracted with Ferrari until the end of the 2027 season, and speaking before this weekend’s US Grand Prix he said he would like to continue racing for at least another four years in order to make it to the meeting in Rwanda.

“I’m now forced to have to stay a lot longer because we have a race in Africa and that’s been my dream to be able to race in Africa,” he said. “So, I have to keep fighting to try and stay fit if I can. If I can still punch out good results over the next year, we’ll keep it going.”
Hamilton would be at least in his mid-40s if he was to continue until 2030. F1’s current oldest driver is 45-year-old Fernando Alonso.

articles.title: Europa League: Celtic lose to Celta after leading, Mateta returns in Palace draw
articles.summary: Sunderland drop points in 1-1 draw but stay unbeaten. VAR rules out Juventus winner in draw with Rennes. Celtic suffered more Europa League pain as Spanish side Celta Vigo came from behind to win 2-1 at Parkhead.
body: Germany midfielder Mika Baur fired the home side in front just over a minute into the second half to thrill the Celtic fans but Spain defender Javi Rodríguez scored twice in three minutes – a header then an unstoppable drive – to stun the home side who could not find a way back.
It was another damaging Euro night for the Scottish champions, knocked out of the Champions League qualifiers by LASK on a 5-4 aggregate after being 4-0 up at one stage earlier in the season.

Celtic’s ultras group, the Green Brigade, boycotted the game in protest at the running of the club, albeit there appeared to be only a couple of hundred empty seats, while 3,000 raucous Celta Vigo fans helped the noise.
Jean-Philippe Mateta scored on his first start since the opening day but Crystal Palace could not capitalise on a Besiktas red card to produce a winner in their 2-2 Europa League draw in Istanbul.

articles.title: Humphries withdraws from European Championship
articles.summary: World number two Luke Humphries pulls out of the European Championship in Germany because of gastroenteritis, with Luke Woodhouse throwing a nine-darter in the opening match of the tournament.
body: Humphries was coming into the tournament on the back of winning the World Grand Prix prior to reaching the final of the Swiss Darts Trophy final, which he lost to Jonny Clayton.
Kim Huybrechts came in as his replacement as the Belgian was the highest-ranked player from the 2026 European Tour rankings who had not qualified.
He took advantage of his late arrival as he produced a dominant 6-1 victory against Ryan Searle during Thursday's first round matches in Dortmund.
Huybrechts hit six 180s and had a 67% checkout success as he set up a second round tie against Stephen Bunting, who produced a 160 checkout in a deciding leg against Danny Noppert as he won 6-5.

articles.title: Bournemouth enjoy night to remember as 10-man Milan fail to weather storm
articles.summary: This was a momentous night in Bournemouth’s history, although the truth is they would have been given a far sterner examination by Coventry or Hull. You can only beat what lies in front of you and Marco Rose’s players never relinquished control against a rotten impersonation of a Milan side.
body: By then Justin Kluivert had given Bournemouth the lead with a penalty and it was another spot-kick from Marcus Tavernier, given after Maignan’s rush of blood, that underlined their overwhelming superiority. Amine Adli applied the garnish with a late free-kick and it meant an abject return to British shores for Ruben Amorim, who would have been excused seeing this particular week as the opportunity to make a point. On this evidence Manchester United, to whom Bournemouth travel on Sunday, share more than a few similarities with the modern version of Milan.

At kick-off the local and broader contexts were impossible to ignore. Bournemouth could hardly have imagined, making their great escape from the fourth-tier trapdoor in 2009, that their modest home would host such a luminous name in a competitive fixture. On the weekend they beat Grimsby, the Rossoneri were overcoming Palermo thanks to goals from Kaká and Filippo Inzaghi. However hard you squinted, seeing the seven-time European champions’ colours on display here felt a trick of the light.

articles.title: Fifa increases preparation money for Women’s World Cup to match men’s teams
articles.summary: Funds for 2027 will match men’s World Cup in 2026. Players given better flights and individual hotel rooms. Teams in the 2027’s Women’s World Cup in Brazil will receive the same preparation money from Fifa as those that played at the 2026 men’s tournament, the world’s governing body has announced.
body: The preparation money for the 32 teams has been more than doubled to $2.5m (£1.86m) each. In 2023, the total preparation money for the tournament was $31m; it will now be $80m.

Every player will be guaranteed business class or chartered flights, as well as their own hotel room rather than having to share. Fifa says this will bring the provisions for the women’s players in line with the men’s World Cup. That is likely be welcomed after the topic caused controversy at previous tournaments.

A survey conducted by the players’ union Fifpro in 2023, after the most recent Women’s World Cup, co-hosted by Australia and New Zealand, found 80% of players’ return flight had been in business class. Ninety-four per cent flew in business class on their outbound flights.

The total prize fund for the tournament is yet to be decided. Fifa has named the United States as the host of the inaugural Women’s Club World Cup in January 2028. The Guardian revealed this month the US was lined up to stage the event, with Los Angeles and San Diego among the favoured host cities.

articles.title: Antonelli to 'just have fun' as he aims for title
articles.summary: Kimi Antonelli says he intends to "just have fun" at the United States Grand Prix as he stands on the brink of the Formula 1 World Championship.
body: This weekend's race in Austin, Texas, is the first time this year the Mercedes driver is mathematically capable of tying up the title.
Antonelli needs to win the race with his team-mate George Russell finishing lower than eighth and Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton below fourth.
"It's crazy if you think about it, but that's why I won't think about it," Antonelli said.
"Something catastrophic to others needs to happen for me to become (champion). For me, needs to be a perfect weekend and to the others they need to do a poor result, which is unlikely to happen.

articles.summary: Como boss Cesc Fabregas rubbed salt into Manchester United’s wounds as he revealed a message he passed on to his players during the 4-1 rout. Embarrassed. United plunged even lower on Wednesday as they were comprehensively beaten by Como at the Giuseppe Sinigaglia Stadium.
body: Nico Paz broke the deadlock inside two minutes before turning provider for Anastasios Douvikas’ second goal of the game, moments after the restart.

Paz completed his brace before the hour mark when he dispossessed Carlos Baleba and charged up the pitch to slot the ball into the bottom corner. Defender Jacobo Ramon made it 4-0 before Joshua Zirkzee netted a consolation goal for United in stoppage time.

United now sit 20th in the Champions League table after their thrashing by Como. The situation is even more dire in the Premier League, where the Red Devils have managed a meagre seven points from their opening seven matches.
A report covered by The Peoples Person relayed that members of the United hierarchy were left shocked and dismayed by the poor performance of the players.

articles.title: Bournemouth seal historic win over Amorim's 10-man Milan
articles.summary: Amine Adli scored a fine free-kick to cap Bournemouth's historic 3-0 win over 10-man AC Milan, which continues their brilliant start to their first-ever European campaign.
body: Ruben Amorim's side are far from the standard of the great Milan teams of the past but this is nonetheless a treasured scalp for Bournemouth who, for the majority of their history, could not have imagined they'd play this fixture. The seven-time European champions, humbled by the Cherries.

It was a wet and wild night on the south coast, with the weather fitting for the chaotic first half, which included Milan captain Mike Maignan being sent off for brutally pushing both hands into Tyler Adams' face at a corner.

That recklessness from the goalkeeper brought Bournemouth their second penalty, which was expertly dispatched by Marcus Tavernier after Justin Kluivert had slotted in the first spot-kick following a Koni De Winter handball.
Another dead-ball moment brought Bournemouth's third. It was a wonderful whip from sub Adli - but Amorim would not have been happy with the Milan wall which broke apart to sum up their sloppiness.

articles.title: Mateta on target as Palace draw with Besiktas in Istanbul
articles.summary: Jean-Philippe Mateta scored his first goal since last season's UEFA Conference League final but Crystal Palace had to settle for a 2-2 draw away at 10-man Besiktas.
body: Mateta thought he had opened the scoring with the first chance of the match when he swept home in the fifth minute, only for VAR to intervene and rule the striker had strayed marginally offside.
Besiktas took the lead against the run of play when Wilfred Ndidi rifled in on the stroke of half-time with Besiktas' first shot on target.

But Palace equalised six minutes after the restart when Pino got on the end of Anan Khalaili's cutback to sweep in. The flag went up for offside, but this time VAR intervened in Palace's favour with the visitors drawing level.
And four minutes later they went ahead after Mateta intercepted a loose back pass before striding into the area and smashing home into the roof of the net.

articles.title: 'That's not enough for me' - Hamilton explains why he went against Ferrari strategy
articles.summary: Lewis Hamilton has explained the reasons why he overrode Ferrari's call to pit in the Singapore Grand Prix, a mistake he says he "owned up to" and will work not to repeat - but which would not prevent him from continuing "challenging the norms".
body: Hamilton dropped out of the podium positions to sixth on worn tyres in the closing stages of the last race at Marina Bay after what proved the costly decision not to pit under the Virtual Safety Car, as the Ferrari pit wall had requested.

Feeling unwell after the gruelling night race, and being excused from his post-race media obligations by the FIA, Hamilton's only comments about his race came via a statement issued by the team and then a post on his Instagram, in which he said he took responsibility for the strategy going wrong.
He spoke in person about what had happened for the first time in Thursday's press conference in Austin ahead of this weekend's United States Grand Prix.

In a detailed answer, Hamilton initially explained why he first chose to start the race on different tyres, the mediums, to team-mate Charles Leclerc who was one place ahead of him on the grid behind Red Bull's polesitting Max Verstappen, the eventual race winner.
